description: Connect your headset to Ethernet with a USB dongle (setup, PD picks, PoE, fixes)

blocks.text: Ethernet-to-USB Dongle on your Quest headset

A USB-C to Ethernet adapter plugged into your headset lets you connect straight to your router, a switch, or your PC. **Adapters with a PD (Power Delivery) port keep the headset charged while you play**, and the connection is usually more stable than Wi-Fi or the USB connection beta.

Meta doesn't officially support this, but they've kept it working and fixed it when it broke in the past.
None of these products are made or endorsed by Virtual Desktop, and none are affiliate links. Buy at your own risk.

pages.name: setup
pages.title: Setup steps
pages.description: How to connect your headset with a dongle

blocks.text:
1. Disable Wi-Fi on your headset.
2. Unplug your headset and turn it off.
3. Connect the Ethernet adapter to the headset's USB-C port. (Short, high-quality USB-C extensions can work, see **Cables & power**.)
4. Plug an Ethernet cable into the adapter and the other end into your router, switch, or PC. Connecting directly to the PC requires ICS, type `/ics` for the guide.
5. If your adapter has a PD port, plug a powered USB-C cable into it.
6. Power on the headset.
7. Confirm it's working by loading a page in the headset's built-in browser.
8. Open Virtual Desktop and connect to your PC.

blocks.name: Good to know
blocks.value:
- The headset shows no Ethernet icon. If it connects with Wi-Fi off, it's working.
- Some adapters (mostly hubs) only work if plugged in while the headset is **off**.
- If Ethernet is your only connection, the headset may not update itself or your apps. Turn Wi-Fi on now and then to update.

pages.name: hubs-poe
pages.title: Hubs & PoE setups
pages.description: Multiport hubs and Power over Ethernet options

blocks.name: Multiport hubs with Ethernet + PD
blocks.value:
Heavier than a dongle, but they work. Several need the headset **off** when you plug them in.
**UGREEN Revodok 6-in-1**: [US](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0BW2TLQ8S) (plug in with headset off)
**NOVOO 7-in-1, 100W PD** (tested on Pico 4/4 Ultra): [DE](https://www.amazon.de/dp/B0957DFS8V)
**Hama 5-port USB-C hub**: [ES](https://www.amazon.es/dp/B08SDVWFHT)
**Acer 9-in-1 USB-C hub**: [US](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0CQSZYWT8)

blocks.name: PoE (power and data over one Ethernet cable)
blocks.value:
A PoE injector or PoE switch sends power down the Ethernet cable, and a PoE-to-USB-C splitter near the headset delivers both. One cable to the headset, no separate charger.
Example kit from a member: REVODATA 2.5GPD2CAT-20V PoE to USB-C (25W) + SODOLA 2.5G PoE+ injector (30W). REVOTECH 25W PoE to Type-C is a cheaper AliExpress option.
Full details and links: [PoE post](https://discord.com/channels/564087419918483486/1553463172818534550/1553471557232361513)

blocks.name: USB-C extensions
blocks.value:
Most people run a short USB-C extension so the dongle isn't hanging off the headset. Keep it short and good quality: long or cheap extensions are the #1 cause of random disconnects.
Reported working: CAKOBLE 3m right-angle [DE](https://www.amazon.de/dp/B0DLNW1T8S) · CHENLENIC 90° 20Gbps [DE](https://www.amazon.de/dp/B0D1V76CYB) · [this setup](https://discord.com/channels/564087419918483486/1390686127937159209/1552346224210743399) (BENFEI + extension + 45W charger)

blocks.name: Power
blocks.value: No special cable needed to power the dongle, any USB-C cable that carries power works. A 20W+ USB-C PD charger is plenty for a Quest. Long 100W C-to-C cables (like Anker's 10ft) are handy for standing play.

blocks.name: Ethernet cable
blocks.value: Use a known-good Cat5e/Cat6 cable. Some cables sold as "Cat 6" only link at 100Mbps, so swap it if your speed tops out around 100.

pages.name: troubleshooting
pages.title: Troubleshooting
pages.description: Slow speeds, disconnects and common gotchas

blocks.name: Test your speed first
blocks.value: Run OpenSpeedTest on your PC (in <#1162377197751906364>) and open it in the headset's browser. You want 900+ Mbps on a gigabit dongle.

blocks.name: Stuck around 100 Mbps
blocks.value: Usually the dongle (wrong chipset, the headset sees it as 100Mb) or a bad Ethernet cable. Try another cable, then a dongle from the tested list.

blocks.name: Good speed test but lag in VD
blocks.value: Cheap dongles can overheat and drop off under sustained load even if a quick speed test looks fine. Reseat/restart the dongle, try Auto bitrate, or switch to a tested dongle.

blocks.name: Random disconnects
blocks.value: Check for a long or low-quality USB extension, or the dongle pigtail wiggling in the headset port. Secure it. If it never happens on Wi-Fi, it's almost certainly the USB side.

blocks.name: Other gotchas
blocks.value:
- On the VD beta, try toggling **Allow USB Connection** off in Settings if your dongle isn't detected.
- Direct-to-PC? Make sure ICS is set to start automatically so it doesn't silently turn off, see `/ics`.
- A switch between PC and headset is fine and can help if your router is busy.

pages.name: other-headsets
pages.title: Other headsets
pages.description: Quest 2/Pro, Pico, Play for Dream, Galaxy XR

blocks.text:
**Quest 2 / Quest Pro**: may need Developer Mode and this adb command from a connected PC:
`adb shell setprop debug.usb.ethernet.enabled 1`

**Pico 4 Ultra, Play for Dream, Galaxy XR**: also support Ethernet adapters, but the steps may differ from the Quest guide.

Meta has removed and restored this feature on Quest 2 and Quest 3 before, so a future update could change things. Check the discussion thread if it suddenly stops working.
